title: Final capstone: multi-page responsive web application using browser storage
learningObjectives: Complete final capstone: multi-page responsive web application using browser storage using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: The capstone combines planning, semantic multi-page structure, reusable responsive styling, JavaScript interactions, browser storage for non-sensitive preferences or progress, accessibility review, and release documentation. It should define scope, data model, navigation, tests, and known limitations.
understand.whyItMatters: A capstone demonstrates integration rather than isolated syntax. Browser storage must not be used for secrets or trusted authorization, and the application should clearly describe what is stored locally.
understand.analogy: The capstone is a complete small product assembled from the skills and components practised throughout the course.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The example persists non-sensitive local progress and theme preferences. A production system requiring cross-device or trusted records needs a backend.

examples.explanation: The example persists non-sensitive local progress and theme preferences. A production system requiring cross-device or trusted records needs a backend.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Build a multi-page learning planner with navigation, lessons, progress, bookmarks, local preferences, keyboard support, tests, README, and deployment checklist.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
